issues.display_title: Issue #523: Map Mode lower-floor visibility — ghost reference walls and area-type context (PRD #504)
issues.main_description_html:
From PRD #504 — part 1 of 3. Improve floor visibility in Map Mode.

Description

  • Render walls from floors below the active floor as a lighter ghost/reference layer in Map Mode, replacing the current merged massing box (geojson-utils.ts:326-350 emits union-of-areas only; lower-floor layout.walls are never emitted)
  • Ghost walls must appear even when disconnected or not attached to any area (today a lower floor with walls but no areas renders nothing)
  • Show simplified lower-floor area-type context: room, hallway, lift, stairs distinguishable; open-to-below rendered as an opening, not a solid surface
  • Reference layers visually lighter than the active floor (opacity/color), never occluding it
  • New layer ids for ghost geometry, excluded from SELECTABLE_LAYERS (useMapSelect.ts) so reference layers are not selectable, hoverable, or labeled

Acceptance Criteria

  • Lower-floor walls appear in Map Mode when floors exist below the active floor
  • Disconnected walls (no matching area) still appear
  • Reference layers are visually lighter than the active floor
  • Open-to-below areas render as openings, not floor surfaces
  • Lower-floor rooms/hallways/lifts/stairs are distinguishable as simplified context
  • Reference layers are not selectable as active-floor objects
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

RESULT

Done on feature/523-ghost-reference-walls, commit 03a2763.

  • geojson-utils.ts — non-active levels emit a ghost reference layer instead of the merged massing box: per-segment wall strips at full configured height (fills the stack to the next floor's base, like the old massing), including walls disconnected from any area — previously invisible. Each area emits a thin slab with areaType preserved (holes cut for contained child areas, same as the active path); open-to-below emits nothing, so it reads as an opening. Shared ring close/winding logic extracted to polysToMultiCoords and reused by the active-area path.
  • layer-definitions.ts — fp-massing-box replaced by fp-ghost-area (per-type color: room cream, hallway white, lift muted blue-grey, stairs muted tan; opacity 0.4) and fp-ghost-wall (wall color, opacity 0.25) — both well below active-layer opacity, rendered before active layers so the active floor always draws on top. Neither is in SELECTABLE_LAYERS, and label/marker paths are already active-level-only, so reference geometry is not selectable, hoverable, or labeled.

Tests: new geojson-ghost.test.ts — ghost walls emitted incl. disconnected, areaType preserved, open-to-below absent, no massing features, active level unaffected. Suite 684 passed, lint + tsc --noEmit clean.

Not pushed — awaiting push + merge approval.

issues.display_title: Issue #524: Ghost wall visibility performance in Map Mode (PRD #504)
issues.main_description_html:
From PRD #504 — part 2 of 3. Keep Map Mode smooth with ghost layers on multi-floor projects.

Description

  • Ghost reference layers (part 1) add per-floor wall/area geometry below the active floor; keep the GeoJSON rebuild and MapLibre layer updates cheap
  • Avoid recomputing lower-floor ghost geometry on every canvasData change that only touches the active floor (memoize per-level ghost features; rebuild only affected levels)
  • Verify smoothness while dragging/rotating/scaling with ghost layers visible (transform path uses setCanvasDataSilent at high frequency)

Acceptance Criteria

  • Map Mode stays smooth on normal multi-floor projects with ghost layers visible
  • Floor switching does not visibly stall with many floors
  • Transform interactions (drag/rotate/scale) stay responsive with ghost layers on
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

RESULT

Done on feature/524-ghost-wall-performance, commit 710046e.

  • geojson-utils.ts — px-space ghost geometry (curve tessellation, directContainment, cutHoles) is now computed once per level and cached in a WeakMap keyed by the level object. The hot path — building drag/rotate/scale pushing setCanvasDataSilent per frame — shallow-spreads canvasData, so level identity is preserved and every frame is a cache hit; only the cheap px→lng/lat projection runs per frame. Real geometry edits replace the level object (immutable store updates), invalidating the cache naturally; mpp is part of the cache guard since it feeds the default wall half-width. spanStrip refactored into spanQuadPx (px math) + projection so both ghost and active paths share one quad implementation.

Tests: 2 new in geojson-ghost.test.ts pinning the cache contract — map-transform changes always move ghost geometry (projection never cached), and a level object with changed geometry recomputes (identity-keyed invalidation). Suite 686 passed, lint + tsc --noEmit clean.

Not pushed — awaiting push + merge approval.

issues.display_title: Issue #525: Floor alignment tools — per-floor transforms with Active/All Floors scope (PRD #504)
issues.main_description_html:
From PRD #504 — part 3 of 3. Floor-level drag, rotate, scale, move, and reset in Map Mode.

Description

  • Add per-level alignment transform (offset/rotation/scale) to LevelData — today all transforms (mapRotationDeg/mapScale/mapOffsetX/Y) are building-wide on canvasData with no per-level hook (geojson-utils.ts:107-127)
  • Apply per-level transform in canvasDataToGeoJson composed with the building transform
  • Scope toggle in the placement tools section: Active Floor vs All Floors; current scope visible before any alignment action
  • Extend MapTransformControl (rotate knob, scale, D-pad, reset) and building drag to respect the scope — Active Floor writes the per-level transform, All Floors keeps writing the building transform
  • Per-floor reset returns only that floor to identity
  • Building-level tools remain available and visually distinct (icons, labels, active states, tooltips)
  • Persistence: per-level transform rides the canvasData blob — no BE change (Go round-trips unknown fields, createdat.go:12-17); survives floor switch, mode switch, reload, save

Acceptance Criteria

  • Active Floor scope moves/rotates/scales/drags only the selected floor
  • All Floors scope moves/rotates/scales/drags all floors together
  • Building controls remain available, clearly separate from floor controls
  • Current scope is visible before any alignment action
  • Per-floor reset affects only that floor
  • Alignment persists across mode change, floor change, reload, and save
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

RESULT

Done on feature/525-floor-alignment-tools, commit 06e1375 (16 files, +356/−61).

  • Data model — LevelData.mapTransform (rotationDeg/scale/offsetX/offsetY), applied in model space about the floor's own footprint center and composed BEFORE the building transform, so aligned floors keep their relative placement when the whole building is later moved/rotated. Absent = identity; reset sets it undefined, which drops out of the saved JSON. Persistence rides the canvasData blob (Go round-trips unknown fields) — no backend change. Engine round-trip safe: modelToLevel spreads ...prev.
  • Geometry — makeLevelPixelTransform(canvasData, levelId) in geojson-utils.ts; canvasDataToGeoJson projects each level (active + ghost) through its own transform. Ghost px cache unaffected — the cache holds pre-transform px space, and per-frame floor drags only replace the dragged level object.
  • UI — placement popup (MapTransformControl) gains an All floors / Active floor scope toggle (store field alignmentScope, ephemeral) with active states and per-scope tooltips; rotate knob, scale pill, D-pad, and reset all target the scoped transform. The bottom-toolbar drag tool and useBuildingDrag are scope-aware too (targetLevelId); map-frame deltas are inverse-rotated/scaled into model space so floor moves follow the cursor on a rotated/scaled building. Building tools keep working exactly as before when scope = All floors.
  • Projection consumers — labels, object markers, preview selection pins, direction route legs (per-leg level), nav-grid debug overlay, dropped pin, pano markers, and pano connections all switched from makePixelRotator to makeLevelPixelTransform, so markers/routes stay attached to aligned floors in editor, preview, and live.

Tests: 6 new in geojson-level-transform.test.ts — offset moves only the target level (active and ghost variants), rotation pivots the floor's own bbox center, level∘building composition order, building-only fallback, JSON round-trip. Suite 692 passed, lint + tsc --noEmit clean.

Not pushed — awaiting push + merge approval.

issues.display_title: Issue #527: feat(projects): integrate Create Empty Project modal (choice screen + create flow)
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Integrates the two-phase "New Project" flow: a choice screen (AI Scanning Floor vs Create Empty Project) and the Create Empty Project modal itself — name, address/label with autocomplete, coordinates, map with drop pin — through to project creation and a direct hand-off into the editor on an empty level.

Scope

Phase 1 — Choice screen

  • Clicking New Project shows two options instead of navigating straight into the wizard: Scan a floor plan and Start from an empty canvas.
  • Wired to every place New Project is offered: dashboard header, dashboard empty state, editor File menu (all route through the same NewProjectFlow component).
  • Dismissible without creating anything.

Phase 2 — Create Empty Project modal

  • Project Name (required, 100-char limit, inline validation on blur).
  • Address / Label field with debounced autocomplete (searchAddressAction), full keyboard support (arrow keys to navigate, Enter to select, Escape to dismiss), closes on outside click.
  • Latitude / Longitude — required, validated (-90..90 / -180..180), placeholder + inline error for both empty and out-of-range values, editable directly.
  • Map with drop pin (MapLibreCore) — moving the map updates coordinates and reverse-geocodes the address; typing coordinates flies the map.
  • Confirm creates the project via the existing createProject → updateProject (isComplete: true) → saveFloorplanAction path, seeds one default empty floor, and redirects straight into /editor/{id}?emptyProject=1 — no scanner/predict call at any point.
  • First-run pointer (EmptyCanvasPointer) points at the wall tool on a freshly created empty level, self-dismisses once geometry exists.
  • Failure keeps the modal open with everything entered and shows a plain error message; retry reuses the already-created project instead of creating a duplicate.

Files touched

  • src/components/projects/NewProjectFlow.tsx — choice screen + modal
  • src/lib/projects/emptyProject.ts — coordinate/name validation, default floor + snapshot builders
  • src/components/editor/EmptyCanvasPointer.tsx — first-run pointer
  • src/components/editor/EmptyProjectPlaceholder.tsx — no-floors editor state
  • src/app/dashboard/page.tsx, src/components/editor/EditorTopbar.tsx — entry points

Verification

  • npx tsc --noEmit — clean
  • npx eslint src/components/projects/NewProjectFlow.tsx — clean
  • Unit tests (emptyProject.test.ts) — passing
  • Publish/share/embed for image-less projects — manually verified, works identically to scanned projects
  • Manual browser run — pending

issues.display_title: Issue #531: Fit Access group copies into the target floor's walls (no out-of-frame overlap)
issues.main_description_html:
Found in project 1536ac63-f014-4a2a-9d81-73e5bc0bcda7 (see screenshot in chat, 2026-08-03).

Description

withAccessSpan() (src/lib/editor/access.ts:144-150) clones a stairs/lift area to newly selected floors with verbatim px boundaries. That assumes every floor shares one coordinate frame. Floors scanned separately have unrelated frames (example project: Floor 1 walls bbox (79,103)–(743,455) vs Floor 2 (27,33)–(179,380)), so the copy lands partly or fully outside the target floor's walls and renders as a stray slab floating outside the building in Map mode — it also inflates the whole-canvas bbox, which shifts/rescales the auto coordSpace and moves the entire building on the map.

Acceptance Criteria

  • A copy created by the floor-span checklist that would fall fully inside the target floor's walls bbox keeps its verbatim geometry (same-frame behavior unchanged)
  • A copy that would poke outside is fitted: uniformly scaled down (never up) to fit the target walls bbox, placed at the same relative position it had in the origin floor's walls bbox, clamped fully inside
  • Target floor without walls: copy keeps verbatim geometry (nothing to overlap)
  • Copies remain ordinary editable areas — the user can still reposition them per floor afterwards
  • Unit tests cover: fits-keeps-verbatim, out-of-frame-gets-fitted, no-walls fallback
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

RESULT

Done on feature/531-fit-access-copies-target-walls, commit 16b2153 (2 files, +128/−1).

  • src/lib/editor/access.ts — new fitBoundaries(template, originLevel, targetLevel) used by withAccessSpan when creating a floor-span copy: verbatim when the geometry already fits inside the target floor's walls bbox (or the target has no walls); otherwise uniformly scaled down (never up) to fit, placed at the template's relative position within the origin frame, clamped fully inside the target walls. Copies remain ordinary editable areas.
  • src/lib/editor/__tests__/access.test.ts — 4 new tests: fits-keeps-verbatim, out-of-frame fitted (inside bbox, aspect preserved, never upscaled, relative quadrant kept), larger-than-frame shrunk to exact fit, no-walls fallback.

Gates: tsc --noEmit clean, eslint clean, full suite 102 files / 708 tests passing.

Note: existing bad copies in saved projects are data — they heal by unchecking/re-checking the floor in Available Levels (recreates the copy through the new fitting), or by manually editing the copy's boundaries.

issues.display_title: Issue #532: Auto-straighten wall drawing — angle snap to H/V/45° and previous segment
issues.main_description_html:
Requested 2026-08-03: walls drawn in the 2D editor come out slightly crooked; drawing should auto-snap to straight.

Description

The wall tool's point resolver (wallPoint(), src/lib/floorplanEditor/editor/interaction-tools.ts) snaps to existing endpoints, wall segments, and the grid, but a freehand segment keeps its raw angle unless Shift (hard H/V lock) is held. Add always-on angle snapping with a tolerance: a segment drawn within 7° of a candidate direction is projected onto it.

  • Candidate directions from the last placed point: global 0°/45°/90°/135° plus parallel and perpendicular of the previous segment in the current chain (deduped)
  • Priority unchanged: endpoint snap → on-wall snap win over angle snap; grid stays composed (H/V results stay grid-aligned, 45° may leave grid)
  • Shift keeps the existing hard H/V lock (wins over auto); holding Alt temporarily disables angle snap
  • Applies to the wall tool and the polygon shape tool (click + preview); curve wall untouched
  • Visual cue while snapped: accent-colored preview segment + thin dashed guide ray

Acceptance Criteria

  • A segment drawn within 7° of horizontal/vertical/45°/135° (or parallel/perpendicular to the previous segment) lands exactly on that direction
  • A segment outside every tolerance is unchanged (freehand still possible)
  • Endpoint and on-wall snapping still take priority over angle snap
  • Shift hard-lock and Alt bypass behave as specified
  • Polygon shape tool gets the same behavior on click and preview
  • Preview shows the snapped state (accent segment + guide ray)
  • Unit tests for the pure snap helper; pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

RESULT

Done on feature/532-wall-angle-snap, 8 commits (7df9f4a..f85170b), head f85170b. Executed via subagent-driven development: per-task implementer + reviewer, final whole-branch review, two review-driven fixes.

  • floorplan/geometry.ts — pure snapAngle(last, p, prevAngle, tolDeg): candidates H/V/45°/135° + previous segment's parallel/perpendicular (deduped), nearest within 7° wins, length-preserving projection, direction-agnostic (drawing leftwards works). 9 unit tests.
  • editor/interaction-tools.ts — wallPoint wires the snap after endpoint/on-wall snaps; Shift keeps the hard H/V lock (beats auto), Alt bypasses. Review fix: the pending ring's first vertex now gets endpoint priority, so near-axis rings stay closable (previously the snap displaced the close click past the 8px tolerance). Priority pinned by wall-point-priority.test.ts (3 tests, mutation-checked).
  • editor/interactions.ts — same snap in polygon shape tool (click + preview) and area tool (click). Close-the-ring tests run before the snap (same endpoint-beats-snap rule). Review fix: Shift (grid quantize) now suppresses the angle snap in polygon draw, so explicit grid intent is never moved off-lattice.
  • editor/draw.ts — cue while snapped: preview strokes turn green (#22c55e) + thin dashed guide ray past the cursor.
  • editor/constants.ts / context.ts / index.ts — ANGLE_SNAP_TOL_DEG = 7, ctx.angleSnap state.
  • Spec + plan committed under docs/superpowers/.

Gates: full suite 104 files / 720 tests passing, lint clean, tsc --noEmit clean.

Known deferrals (final review triaged all as non-blocking): polygon/area close-priority has no pinned regression test (wall does); angleSnap.angle payload unread in production (could be boolean); guide-ray block duplicated twice in draw.ts; diagonal snaps may leave the grid when grid snap is on (accepted in spec).
